messages:
maria: Pushing a canary driver upgrade to eu-west-1 now: nvidia-driver 535.60 -> expected to finish rollout by 12:45 UTC. small batch of h100 pods first. tagging canary with alloc=canaeu1

sanjay: Got it. Monitoring GPU allocs and nccl health. Will watch traces and p99 latency.

ops-bot: deploy: canary group 'canaeu1' updated to driver 535.60 (4 nodes)

kevin: Seeing increased TensorRT kernel failures on the canary nodes, some inference containers falling back to slower kernels. Sample from pod gpu-rt-7:
```
ERROR: TensorRT failed to load kernel for plugin flash_attn_bwd: PTX rejected: ptx_arch=90, compiled_ptx=86, cubin: reject_reason=unknown_ptx_version
stack: trt_infer.cpp:420
```

maria: Oof. That looks like PTX arch mismatch. Which model/profile?

kevin: 70% of failing requests are bert-large/seq1024 streaming route (high batch). CNTK batch size 8. We'll see fallback to reference kernels and throughput drops ~3x.

natalie: NCCL also throwing some WARNs during scheduled rolling drain:
```
WARN nccl: allreduce failed with error UNIMPLEMENTED on rank 2, fallback to LL128 path
```

sanjay: Correlating: when a pod hits trt kernel reject it spikes CPU, causing kube-probe flaps and then nccl reconnect chatter. Impacted pods then routed to slower nodes -> latency p99 jumps.

maria: Pause the expansion of the canary. Rollback policy? Can we pin these nodes back to 535.54?

kevin: We can rollback driver on the 4 canary hosts quickly. Alternative short-term mitigation: set env var in runtime to disable flashattention JIT so TRT uses portable kernel path:
```
env: DISABLE_FLASH_ATTN_JIT=1
```
But that will increase token cost/latency.

dawn: Cost note: if we keep canary running with fallback kernels we'll burn ~2.5x GPU minutes for affected routes. If this hits production fractionally that'll hit monthly usage budgets. Recommend rollback for now, open bug with vendor.

maria: Agreed. sanjay, can you rollback the 4 hosts and stop the canary rollout? Also collect ptx logs and cubin rejects for NV ticket.

sanjay: On it. Rolling back drivers now. Command used:
```bash
ssh node-122 sudo apt install -y nvidia-driver=535.54
systemctl restart nvidia-persistenced
# wait for GPU health checks
kubectl drain node-122 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```
I'll gather /var/log/nvidia-installer.log and the trt logs from pods.

kevin: I pulled a few trt logs and attached trimmed stack in the issue. Also note that the canary nodes are using AMI image h100-ubuntu-2024-09 with CUDA 12.4 runtime. Looks like the new driver is producing newer PTX that flashattn (precompiled) doesn't accept.

nvidia-eng: Thanks for the heads up — we'll create a ticket with PTX rejects and cubin. Please include output of:
```bash
nvidia-smi -q | grep -E "Driver Version|CUDA Version"
cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version
```
and the trt plugin build flags.

maria: sanjay, status?

sanjay: Rollback completed on 4 canary nodes at 12:32 UTC. Pods recovered, p99 back to baseline in ~3 min. I'm pausing the cluster driver rollout. Created internal incident and assigned to eng-runtime.

ops-bot: incident: INC-2024-117 created ("eu-west driver canary: TRT/flashattn ptx rejects") assigned to eng-runtime, priority P2

kevin: Opening a short-term playbook item: when upgrading drivers we should run a lightweight kernel-compat smoke that: 1) loads TRT plugins, 2) runs a 2-step assembly compile of flashattn plugin, 3) runs an nccl allreduce test across 2 nodes. We failed to exercise PTX JIT path pre-rollout.

dawn: Agreed. Also add cost gating: if fallback slow-path expected >1.5x cost increase for a route, auto-hold rollout.

maria: Action items:
- sanjay: upload logs and rollback notes to INC-2024-117 (done)
- kevin: draft compatibility smoke and add to canary checklist (ETA EOD)
- dawn: add cost-threshold hold to rollout automation (ETA 48h)
- kevin: open vendor ticket and attach PTX/cubin + driver build info (ETA 2h)

natalie: For the long term we should consider building precompiled TRT kernels for the flashattn plugin targeting PTX arch permutations we support so runtime JIT is less necessary. That will save startup jitter too.

nvidia-eng: We'll triage with driver team. Please include reproducer + ptx rejects and we'll advise if driver micro-release required or if plugin rebuild is needed.

maria: Thanks all. Reopening canary only after compatibility smoke added and vendor signoff if needed. :thumbsup:
